newsitem.title: UK: Ad execs doubt effectiveness of their work--survey.
newsitem.headline: Ad execs doubt effectiveness of their work--survey.

text.p: Fewer than one-third of advertising professionals responding to a survey believe that the advertising they produce works for their clients, a trade publication reported on Thursday.

Campaign magazine, which surveyed 600 employees from the top 50 advertising agencies in London, said that of the respondents who actually plan and evaluate the success of advertising campaigns, the belief in the effectiveness of their advertising campaigns fell to below 20 percent of respondents.

"It is staggering to think that so many people in advertising believe that their efforts are falling short of the mark," Campaign editorial director Dominic Mills said in a statement. "Part of this can be blamed on frustration with many advertisers requesting safe and predictable advertising solutions."

The survey also found that most respondents said drug-taking is commonplace in the industry. Sexism was ranked as the industry's greatest prejudice -- cited by 40 percent of women and 32 percent of men -- and racism was said to be prevalent by up to 30 percent of employees.
